solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Support broadcast letters

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so what follows gets strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Letters sent out on the airwaves as a show of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast letters' reads like radio messages, but broadcast is the anagram signal and the fodder is the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs and a crossbar that holds up a table top, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: A group of alcoholics including bishops

indicators.note: a group including someone has them inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A support meeting of drinkers that counts some clergy among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition swallows the clue's opening 'A': the answer is a group, and the setter cheekily calls it 'A group'.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA was the Swedish pop band famous for Waterloo and Dancing Queen, so it is a musical group.

clue.text: Fool around — tool cut by date, twice

indicators.note: a thing cut by something is split open with that something lodged in the gap

parts.note: a file is a metalworking tool
D is the abbreviation for date, taken twice

explanation.surface: Someone messing about with a tool, distracted by a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' tells you to double the abbreviation before it goes inside the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to fidget or mess about aimlessly, an informal synonym for fooling around.

clue.text: Uses cooks around North after cold count

indicators.note: coming after means following, so this piece is placed behind the one before it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: being around something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another
to cook is to doctor or fiddle, as with cooked books, so the letters are tampered with

parts.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cook making use of ingredients from the north, after something cold — a kitchen tally.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged word wraps the compass point, and the whole lot follows the tap abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population, so the noun count fits it as a direct synonym.

clue.text: Composition of party foregone conclusion — zilch!

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative party
a cert is a certainty, something bound to happen
zilch is nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: A party's makeup was a done deal, and nothing came of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition of party' looks like a membership list, but composition is the definition and 'of' just joins it. CERT is British slang for a dead certainty, a racing term.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a piece of music for soloist and orchestra, an example of a musical composition.

clue.text: Sun: hollow rivalry with our mag — ultimately absurd and unrealistic

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: something hollow has had its insides scooped out, leaving only the shell at each end

parts.note: only the first and last letters stay
the setter writes for Private Eye, so our magazine is the Eye

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A dig at The Sun newspaper's empty rivalry with Private Eye, dismissed as absurd and fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the tabloid, which suits the surface, but here it is the celestial body. 'Our mag' only works because the puzzle runs in Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone starry-eyed is naively idealistic, dreamily ignoring practical facts, so the adjective matches unrealistic.

clue.text: Appeals of actors experiencing change of political allegiance?

indicators.note: switching political sides means going from the Left to the Right, so one wing's letter is swapped for the other's

parts.note: players are actors in a theatre company

explanation.surface: Pleas from thespians who have defected from one party to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The political defection is Left to Right, so the L of the actors becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Prayers are requests made to God, solemn entreaties, so they are appeals in the sense of earnest pleas.

clue.text: Talk of bra stuffed with small coin

indicators.note: in British slang something stuffed is ruined or done for, so the letters end up wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is an old word for a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Gossip about a bra padded out with a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed with' reads as filling one thing with another, but no container works; the bra and the coin are jumbled together. To rabbit on is British slang for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, means to chatter on at length.

clue.text: From whom there's news Brenda's back on the drink

indicators.note: placed on means set beside, so one part sits next to the next
going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Gossip that the Queen has started drinking again.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda', so she gives ER; and 'the drink' is not just booze but a specific beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and delivers stories, so they are the source of news.

clue.text: Wheeler-dealer lifted old Communist paintings

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting something raises it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: Red is an old name for a Communist
paintings are art

explanation.surface: A dodgy dealer who stole an old Soviet's art collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' reads as stolen, which suits the dealer, but in a down clue it turns the letters upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeler-dealer is a shrewd operator doing business deals, and a trader buys and sells for profit.

clue.text: Seeks to be an MP, holding right to be in ad for British newspapers?

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a candidate stands for Parliament

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so this letter goes within the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A would-be MP keeps the right to place an advert in the British press.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the single letter sits inside the advert, and that pair sits inside the candidate's verb. The Evening Standard is a London paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags an example: the Evening Standard and other papers bearing the name are newspapers called Standards.

clue.text: Old party leader sees off his last Midland town

indicators.note: to see off is to get rid of, so a letter is dismissed

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn, former Labour Party leader
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A former party boss gets rid of his last supporters in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His last' points back to the leader's own name, so his final letter goes. Corby is a steel town in Northamptonshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Corby is a former steel-making town in Northamptonshire, which lies in the East Midlands region of England.

clue.text: Slip makes genital area extremely sore

parts.note: the lap is the area of the thighs and groin when seated

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are kept

parts.note: just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cringe-making sentence about an underwear slip chafing the nether regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' sounds like underwear in this surface, but it is the definition, meaning an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a brief failure of attention or judgement, so it is a slip in the sense of a small mistake.

clue.text: Marketing video going to new politician's head

indicators.note: going to means joining up with, so one part is followed by the next

parts.note: a promo is a promotional video
N is the abbreviation for new
a Tory is a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A slick campaign video that goes straight to a fresh MP's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Politician's head' looks like a phrase about ego, but the possessive just links the politician to the definition, which is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is high land jutting into the sea, and head is a geographic term for such a headland.

clue.text: Buck suppresses story about being a vandal

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a buck is a male deer

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or knocked about, so the letters are moved out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man hushes up an account of his own vandalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a verb or a dollar, but it is the male animal, which then wraps the reworked tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal wrecks property on purpose, and a destroyer is anyone who ruins or demolishes things.

clue.text: Good place to see stars getting oddly sober on toilet (LA excepted)

indicators.note: placed on means put next to, so one part is set beside the other
done oddly means done in a strange, irregular way, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: excepted means left out, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: a lavatory is a toilet
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Hollywood stars sobering up in the loo — anywhere but Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' usually means take odd letters, but here it is the anagram signal; LA is not Los Angeles but two letters to strip from the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An observatory is a building fitted with telescopes for watching the night sky, so it is an ideal spot for seeing stars.

clue.text: Rank material by TV presenter

indicators.note: by means beside, so one part is placed next to the other

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woven fabric
Ant McPartlin, of the British TV duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A smelly costume worn by a television host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul, describing the material, but it is the definition in its military sense. Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British presenting pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer grade in the army or police, so it names a particular rank.

clue.text: Say mule ditching drug possibly gets state protection

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements, so the letters may be reordered
ditching something means dumping it, so a letter is thrown out

parts.note: taken as written
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug courier who dumps the stash and is then granted refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mule' fits the surface as a drug smuggler, but here it is just letters to shuffle once the ecstasy is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is the shelter a country grants to refugees fleeing persecution, legal protection given by a nation.

clue.text: Raise leg to get an advantage on the boards

definitions.text: get an advantage on the boards

parts.note: to up something is to raise it, as in upping prices
a leg of a journey or race is a stage

explanation.surface: A dancer lifts a leg to steal the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise leg' reads as a physical move, but each word is a synonym in turn; 'the boards' is an old phrase for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage is to move behind a fellow actor, forcing them to face away from the audience, and so steal attention in the theatre.

clue.text: Fake, artificially pert rear

indicators.note: artificially means not naturally, so the letters are set out in an unnatural order

parts.note: taken as written
the end is the rear of something

explanation.surface: A bottom that looks perky only thanks to cosmetic help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' plays on bottoms in the surface but is just the back end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretend and fake both work as adjectives meaning not genuine, imitation, so they swap directly.

clue.text: In favour of dutiful conduct, maintaining the ultimate in regular decency

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep and hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: piety is dutiful devotion, to God or parents

indicators.note: the ultimate in something is its very end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Praise for well-behaved people who keep up standards of respectability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' is not a selection signal for alternate letters here; it is the source word, and only its last letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety means conformity to accepted standards of behaviour, which is what decency describes.

clue.text: During sex, hum 'Emotion' and move the body

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the answer lies within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone humming a song called Emotion mid-sex and swaying to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move the body' reads as dancing, but the body here is a corpse dug up from the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a buried corpse out of the ground, so it literally relocates a dead body.

clue.text: (& 26dn.) Obliged to be truthful around the ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, as in ground coffee, so the letters are broken down and reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness bound to tell the truth about the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' tempts as a container signal and 'ground' as land, but the two short words before it are themselves the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness under oath has sworn a solemn promise in court, so they are legally bound to tell the truth.

clue.text: Rough venue, kinky name

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A seedy club with a suggestive name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough venue' reads as a dive bar, but 'Rough' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough surface is bumpy rather than smooth, so uneven is an adjectival synonym for it.

clue.text: Lady's boob on live entertainment debut?

indicators.note: on means placed against, so one part sits beside the other

parts.note: slang for a breast

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so each word contributes its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction on stage on opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady's' looks possessive, but it means Lady is: the definition, then the wordplay. Boob also means blunder, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is an honorific given to the wife of a lord or a peeress, so it is a form of rank prefixed to a name.

clue.text: Crafty thing has MPs seated next to snake (Tory leader)

indicators.note: next to means beside, so the pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: the sitting MPs make up the House of Commons
a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A cunning operator seats MPs beside a snake of a Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' reads as cunning, but it means craft-like: a vessel on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a boat fitted out as a home, and boats are water craft, so it is a punning crafty thing.

clue.text: see 23ac.
Extremely lacking, Lord Gnome collapsed with "Independence" war cry

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen to pieces, so the letters fall into a new order
lacking the extremes means losing both ends, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the inner letters
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for independence

explanation.surface: Private Eye's proprietor Lord Gnome falls over with a cry for independence.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional proprietor; only the first word loses its ends, and the quotation marks around the capital I word dress up a plain abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo is the cry paratroopers shout as they jump, named after the Apache leader, so it is a battle shout.

clue.text: Elton put away inside, hammered

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Ben Elton, the British comedian and writer
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Elton John jailed and drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Elton suggests Elton John, but it is the surname of comedian Ben Elton, and the clue supplies his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten and hammered both mean soundly defeated or struck repeatedly, so the past participles swap directly.
